title: AWS DevOps Agent
strapline: Incident investigation, service-status analysis and release-readiness workflows.
audience: On-call engineers, SREs, platform engineers and service owners
availability: Production operations: GA. Release management: preview; assess each feature and Region separately.
decision: Start with one read-heavy investigation workflow. Add action paths only after the evidence and authorization boundaries have been tested.
summary: During an incident, the hard part is rarely opening another dashboard. It is connecting the affected service, the deployment that preceded the symptom, and the evidence that distinguishes a plausible explanation from the actual failure. DevOps Agent brings those sources into an investigation context; the engineer still decides whether the evidence justifies a mitigation.

This report follows an illustrative checkout failure after a retry-policy change. The useful result is not a fluent root-cause statement. It is a traceable investigation, a controlled next action, and a verification record. The same context can support daily health questions and prevention work. Release-readiness review and active release testing are a distinct preview path, not a capability that becomes generally available merely because production operations are GA.

use_case.name: Checkout errors after a retry-policy release
use_case.trigger: A supplied incident snapshot shows rising checkout 5xx errors after deployment DEMO-A.
use_case.scope: One team-owned service, explicit environment and UTC incident window, selected repositories and telemetry.
use_case.deliverable: Evidence-backed incident handoff with a mitigation candidate, owner, rollback assumptions and recovery checks.
use_case.not_done: The agent has written a plausible explanation, but the deployed revision and telemetry have not been compared.
use_case.done: The service owner has accepted or rejected the explanation, authorized any change separately, and recorded independent recovery evidence.

stages.title: Establish the operational boundary
paragraphs: Begin with the service and the incident window, not an unrestricted instruction to fix production. An Agent Space gathers account configuration, integrations and application context. Its topology helps the investigation understand relationships; underlying IAM and integration permissions determine what can actually be accessed.

Connect a known-good deployment reference and the telemetry needed to challenge the incident hypothesis. Missing logs are an evidence gap, not a reason to grant broad write permissions. Validate one expected read and one harmless out-of-scope denial before relying on the configuration.
stages.input: Service identity, environment, incident window, deployed revision, relevant telemetry and repository access.
stages.artifact: A scope record and a short inventory of available and missing evidence.
stages.gate: The service owner can explain the access boundary and identify who can stop the work.
stages.fallback: Keep the incident in the normal on-call process while missing evidence or permissions are repaired.

stages.title: Investigate, then challenge the explanation
paragraphs: An alert, ticket or on-demand question can start the operational workflow. Ask the agent to separate observations, hypotheses and missing data. For the checkout example, the deployment time, affected resources and request failures need to agree before the change becomes the leading explanation.

Use follow-up questions to test alternatives: an upstream timeout, a capacity limit, or an unrelated configuration change. A confident answer does not eliminate competing causes. The engineer compares material claims with the source systems and preserves the evidence links for the incident record.
stages.input: Incident signal and scoped operational context.
stages.artifact: A hypothesis ledger with supporting observations, contrary evidence and unresolved gaps.
stages.gate: At least one material claim is independently checked against its source.
stages.fallback: Record an inconclusive investigation rather than inventing a cause or waiting indefinitely.

stages.title: Separate a recommendation from an authorized action
paragraphs: A mitigation proposal should state the intended effect, blast radius, validation criteria and reversal plan. In the example, reducing retries may be a candidate, but a service owner must consider whether it hides errors or shifts load elsewhere. Recommendations are reviewable artifacts, not implicit permission to modify resources.

Directed actions have their own enablement, access and approval controls. Keep the action decision attached to the exact target and operation. An approval to investigate is not approval to deploy, and a broad instruction in chat is not a substitute for the configured authorization path.
stages.input: Reviewed hypothesis and a specific mitigation candidate.
stages.artifact: An action decision with owner, target, allowed effect, rollback and verification criteria.
stages.gate: The effect is authorized through the correct product and team controls.
stages.fallback: Execute through the established runbook or change process when the agent action path is not approved.

stages.title: Turn an incident into owned prevention work
paragraphs: After recovery, recurring incident patterns can inform observability, resilience, infrastructure and deployment improvements. Convert a useful recommendation into a bounded engineering item rather than leaving it as an unowned report. Preserve the original incident references so the proposed fix can be evaluated against the actual failure.

Daily health summaries are configured custom-agent workflows. Specify the question, tools, skills, schedule and audience explicitly. A scheduled prompt cannot see a database or monitoring system that has not been connected, and an automated summary still needs an owner who handles missing or stale data.
stages.input: Validated incident record, historical incidents and a named follow-up owner.
stages.artifact: A prioritized improvement item or configured recurring operational report.
stages.gate: The item has measurable acceptance criteria and the scheduled output has a recipient and stop owner.
stages.fallback: Use the existing backlog and manual report until the integrations provide adequate evidence.

stages.title: Review the next release without confusing the test paths
paragraphs: The follow-up retry-policy change can be reviewed for release risk. Readiness review evaluates a code change and its dependencies, policies and access implications; managed verification can add build or test evidence. These are release-preview features and should be piloted separately from the production investigation baseline.

Active release testing instead interacts with a running application. Browser or API requests can create, update or delete data and trigger business effects. Use a disposable staging target, test identities and disabled external side effects. Infrastructure write access being disabled does not make application testing read-only.
stages.input: Candidate revision, application context, and an authorized staging target where active testing is used.
stages.artifact: Release findings, reproduction details and explicit residual risks.
stages.gate: The release owner checks both feature availability and the actual effects allowed against the test target.
stages.fallback: Use prepared results or the ordinary test suite rather than testing a production endpoint to keep a demo moving.

stages.title: Hand off an operational work item and verify closure
paragraphs: The proposed team handoff turns an accepted investigation into an owned engineering work item. Include the incident window, affected service and revision, evidence references, remaining uncertainty and the required recovery check. Preparing a code or configuration change is a responsibility of the receiving engineering team; it is not an additional DevOps Agent capability claimed here.

Use the existing review and delivery process for any change. The service owner checks current telemetry after deployment, records whether the symptom recovered and reopens the investigation when the evidence does not support closure. A generated recommendation alone is not a completed incident.
stages.input: Evidence-linked issue with affected repository, constraints, test expectations and reviewer.
stages.artifact: Reviewed code or operational change plus a recovery or regression-test record.
stages.gate: A human reviewer accepts the result; deployment authority and access remain local to their own systems.
stages.fallback: Keep a failed or inconclusive change visible as unfinished work rather than closing the incident on generated text.

checks: One owned workload and UTC time window are recorded.
A deployed revision and material telemetry are available.
Out-of-scope access is denied at the actual integration layer.
Hypotheses and missing evidence are separated.
Any change has its own authorization, rollback and verifier.
Active release tests use an approved non-production target.
